expectations.text: The response separates stated project facts from repository facts that still need inspection and avoids claiming that the migration, tests, Unity Editor, or profiling were executed.
expectations.evidence: The context explicitly separates "User-stated", "Observed" absence of repository/editor/build/profile evidence, and working assumptions. The verification section says no tests, Unity compilation, build, migration, or profiling were run.

expectations.text: The target design decomposes the GameManager into feature-scoped responsibilities with explicit composition roots, dependency direction, and component/scene/session lifetimes rather than replacing it with another global manager.
expectations.evidence: The target diagram defines ApplicationRoot, SessionScope, SceneCompositionRoot, views/adapters, and inward dependency direction. The lifetime table covers application, session, scene, and encounter/actor ownership, and the response explicitly warns against six globally accessible replacement managers.

expectations.text: Shared ScriptableObject assets are treated as authored definitions, while mutable session/runtime state receives an explicit owner, reset policy, and persistence boundary.
expectations.evidence: The ScriptableObject section makes assets read-only authored definitions, creates plain SessionState in SessionScope from their values, discards it on return to menu, and maps it through a versioned save DTO. It also rejects dual writable sources of truth and specifies ownership/destruction for any necessary runtime clone.

expectations.text: The migration is incremental and behavior-preserving, beginning with characterization tests and naming safe slices, compatibility seams, rollback points, and verification before old paths are removed.
expectations.evidence: The seven-stage strangler plan begins with characterization and diagnostics, keeps GameManager behind LegacyGameRuntimeAdapter, moves one authoritative capability at a time, names rollback behavior for early slices, and removes the shell only after inventory and lifecycle gates pass.

expectations.text: The design introduces plain C# domain/application seams and acyclic assembly-definition boundaries only where they improve testability or team ownership, with Unity adapters at the edges.
expectations.evidence: It places session/combat rules and use cases in plain C# domain/application assemblies, keeps input/audio/save/scene/view concerns in Unity adapters, gives an acyclic assembly graph, avoids a broad Common assembly, and says to split assemblies only for real change/team or compilation boundaries.

expectations.text: Manual composition, a DI container, Service Locator, and ECS/DOTS are compared proportionally; container/ECS adoption is rejected unless concrete graph complexity or measured scale justifies the cost.
expectations.evidence: Manual composition is selected for its explicit/reversible graph; Service Locator is rejected as hidden global access. DI requires repeated non-trivial scoped graphs plus a target-compatible spike, and ECS/DOTS requires a measured homogeneous simulation bottleneck plus a representative prototype.

expectations.text: Additive-scene readiness, stale listener cleanup, initialization, teardown, return-to-menu, and repeated load/unload tests are explicitly addressed.
expectations.evidence: The scene coordinator waits for explicit destination readiness before retiring the prior scope and cleans partially loaded destinations on failure. The UI contract defines Initialize/Start/Stop/Dispose; the plan and gates cover stale listeners, repeated additive load/unload, disable/enable, cancellation, and boot -> game -> additive UI -> unload -> return to menu -> new game.

expectations.text: Performance and scalability claims remain hypotheses until a representative target build is profiled with a reproducible baseline.
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly rejects code-shape speed claims, requires a representative player/build and same-content target procedure before and after any performance claim, and makes measured target-device pressure a prerequisite for ECS/DOTS or other optimization.

claims.claim: The recommended target is a manual-composition strangler migration with GameManager retained temporarily as a compatibility shell.
claims.evidence: The Decision, target architecture, and staged migration all consistently specify that design.

claims.claim: The stale UI listener symptom is caused by missed unsubscription rather than duplicate roots, late async completion, or a static publisher.
claims.evidence: The artifact explicitly presents all four as unresolved candidates and requires characterization; no repository or runtime evidence was available.

claims.claim: The final artifact does not present the migration or its verification gates as executed.
claims.evidence: It explicitly states that tests, Unity compilation, builds, migration, and profiling were not run. No transcript exists to independently verify executor behavior beyond the artifact.

claims.claim: The proposed assembly and lifetime boundaries are incremental rather than an assembly-first rewrite.
claims.evidence: The plan introduces assemblies only around extracted code, retains legacy-side adapters, and supplies capability-level exit and rollback gates.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set exercises the material architectural, lifecycle, migration, testability, proportionality, and evidence-quality decisions; no significant untested outcome was apparent.
